https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europ.text: Hungarian music showcase Ozora Festival cut short after two deaths Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox Published Aug 02, 2026, 08:11 PM Updated Aug 02, 2026, 09:06 PM Set as preferred source Listen Summarise The Ozora Festival in Hungary ended early after two deaths: an American man fell to his death and a Hungarian woman died of a heart attack. The man likely took his own life by climbing a set piece and falling, while the woman suffered a medical emergency, probably due to extreme heat. Organisers stopped all music programmes early and expressed condolences amid a heatwave with temperatures reaching 40 deg C in Hungary. AI generated Budapest – A music festival held in central Hungary is to end earlier than scheduled, organisers said on Aug 2 , after an American man fell to his death and a young woman died of a heart attack. The one-week Ozora Festival, described as one of the largest global psychedelic trance gatherings, attracts tens of thousands each year. On Aug 1 , a 45-year-old American man climbed onto one of the set pieces surrounding the main stage and then plunged to the ground, fatally, police told local news site FEOL. The authorities and organisers said they believed the man likely took his own life intentionally. Earlier that day, a 39-year-old Hungarian woman suffered a medical emergency, “probably due to the intense heat”, and attempts to resuscitate her were unsuccessful, according to FEOL. “In light of these tragic events, all music programmes will end at midnight tonight, including those at the Pumpui stage,” organisers said on Facebook, offering their condolences. Aug 2 was the last full day of the festival, but music performances on the Pumpui stage were previously scheduled to last until the early morning of Aug 3 . Hungary has been under its highest heat alert since July 30 , with maximum temperatures reaching 40 deg C over this weekend. http://www.asiabulletin.com/news/2792529.text: Jaishankar greets Hungary on National Day; looks forward to strengthening bilateral ties ANI 20 Aug 2026, 10:28 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], August 20 (ANI): External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Thursday extended greetings to the Government and people of Hungary on the country's National Day, saying he looked forward to further strengthening bilateral ties. In a post on X, Jaishankar said, 'Warm greetings to the Government and people of Hungary on their National Day. Look forward to further strengthening our ties.' https://x.com/DrSJaishankar/status/2090272109553725581 August 20 is observed as Hungary's State Foundation Day, commemorating the establishment of Christian Hungarian statehood in 1000 AD and honouring King Saint Stephen, the country's first monarch and founder. Along with the post, the image accompanying it highlighted the celebration of the International Day of Yoga in Hungary in June 2026, with the participation of the local community. The text in the image said, 'The International Day of Yoga was celebrated in Hungary with the participation of the local community (June 2026).' August 20 is defined as the official State Foundation Day of Hungary. It legally commemorates the establishment of the Christian Hungarian statehood over a millennium ago in the year 1000 AD, honouring the legacy of King Saint Stephen, the nation's first monarch and founder. Earlier in May, Jaishankar extended greetings to Anita Orban on her appointment as the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Hungary. In a post on X, he said, 'Congratulations to Anita Orban on her appointment as the Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister of Hungary. Look forward to working together to strengthen the India-Hungary relationship and the India-EU strategic partnership.' On May 9, Hungary's new government officially took office. Prime Minister Peter Magyar and his new cabinet were sworn in following the landslide victory of the Tisza Party in the parliamentary elections held on April 12. On that day, Orban called the election a new chapter in Hungary. In a post on X, she said, 'A new chapter begins in Hungary today. The inaugural session of the new Parliament is underway. Representatives have taken their oath, followed by an address from President Tamas Sulyok. Soon, Parliament will elect a new Speaker, and later today, Peter Magyar is expected to be elected Prime Minister by open vote. Outside, on Kossuth Square, thousands are gathering, following every moment together. It is no coincidence that this day falls on Europe Day. The message is clear: Hungary's place is in Europe. Naturally, firmly, and without question. And with that comes responsibility. The real work begins today.' India's relations with Hungary have been close and friendly, multifaceted, and substantive. They have survived the vicissitudes of political and economic changes, particularly in Hungary and the reorientation of its foreign policy in the post-Cold War period. Hungarians are extremely grateful for India's role in the 1956 uprising in Hungary. External Affairs Minister Jaishankar visited Hungary from 25 to 27 August 2019. During his visit, EAM held discussions with Hungary's Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto on a wide range of bilateral and multilateral issues. The two Ministers signed a Cultural Exchange Programme between India and Hungary for the period 2019-22. The Hungarian side announced its decision to join the International Solar Alliance. Five main areas of film production, digitalisation, water management, solar energy, and pharmaceuticals were identified for strengthening cooperation. https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text: A police statement said: ‘Officers attended the scene alongside the London ambulance service and London’s air ambulance and found four men with stab wounds.’ Photograph: James Manning/PA View image in fullscreen A police statement said: ‘Officers attended the scene alongside the London ambulance service and London’s air ambulance and found four men with stab wounds.’ Photograph: James Manning/PA London Four people in hospital after stabbing in south-east London Seven people arrested following ‘altercation’ on Bromley High Street on Thursday afternoon Emine Sinmaz and Kevin Rawlinson Thu 10 Sep 2026 14.07 EDT First published on Thu 10 Sep 2026 12.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Seven people have been arrested after four men were stabbed in south-east London , the Metropolitan police said. Officers were called to reports of “an altercation” on Bromley High Street at 2.15pm and found four men with stab wounds, the force added. In a statement, it said: “Officers attended the scene alongside the London ambulance service and London’s air ambulance and found four men with stab wounds. Three of them were taken to hospital where they are receiving treatment for non-life-threatening injuries. One is in critical condition. View image in fullscreen Forensic investigators at the scene on Thursday afternoon. Photograph: James Manning/PA “Seven men were arrested and they all remain in custody. Police inquiries continue and there is not believed to be any wider threat to the public.” A cordon was in place at the scene on Thursday, with police, as well as community support officers, standing around the perimeter. Forensics officers dressed in blue overalls and a crime scene photographer were coming and going from a branch of KFC, where locals said the incident occurred, and there were evidence markers visible on the floor. Abandoned food could still be seen on the tables as evening drew in, suggestive of the haste in which people left the restaurant amid the incident. “I heard a really loud bang and people running from KFC,” said George Ioannou, who was working in Antonio’s Male Grooming next door to the KFC. “An elderly woman ran into the shop and I had to lock the door to shelter her until it calmed down. She was crying. About five minutes later, we heard the sirens.” Other shop workers nearby said the incident was quick and that it was over in moments. The KFC has an alleyway down one side – along which people ran as they passed the male grooming shop – and faces on to Bromley’s High Street. Part of the latter was still closed to the public on Thursday evening. It is a busy thoroughfare, with a large shopping centre at one end and a train station taking commuters between Kent, south-east London and the capital’s centre at the other. Those and the parade of shops lining the high street draw large numbers of people from the surrounding area. About 15 bus routes were diverted, including the 61, 208 and 119. The London ambulance service said ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast-response car, an incident response officer, an advanced paramedic and London’s air ambulance were dispatched to the scene. Four patients were treated at the scene before being taken to hospital, the service added. The Bromley and Biggin Hill MP Peter Fortune said: “I am aware of the incident on Bromley High Street this afternoon and I know that residents will have safety concerns. The police are in attendance and have made a number of arrests. I will remain in close contact with the police as they continue to investigate this incident.” A picture shared on social media on Thursday afternoon appeared to show a section of Bromley High Street cordoned off, with an emergency vehicle on site. The Met asked anyone with information to contact the police on 101. http://www.torontotelegraph.com/news/279.text: Canada advances defence partnerships in Poland Canada News Centre 10 Sep 2026, 23:50 GMT+10 September 10, 2026 - Kielce, Poland - Global Affairs Canada This week, the Honourable Maninder Sidhu, Minister of International Trade, joined the Honourable David J. McGuinty, Minister of National Defence, at the International Defence Industry Exhibition (MSPO), held from September 8 to 11, 2026, in Kielce, Poland, to promote Canada's defence industry, as well as to deepen Canada's trade relationships with Poland and across Europe. Canada and Poland are strengthening ties in defence, trade, advanced technologies and energy security, and, as North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) Allies, are united in supporting collective defence and transatlantic security. Minister Sidhu kicked off his visit to Poland in Warsaw by meeting with Andrzej Domaski, Minister of Finance and Economy. They discussed opportunities to expand Canada-Poland commercial collaboration in priority sectors such as defence, energy and aerospace. Minister Sidhu also met with both Miosz Motyka, Minister of Energy, and Wojciech Wrochna, Plenipotentiary for Strategic Energy Infrastructure and Secretary of State at the Ministry of Energy, to champion Canada as one of the world's most reliable suppliers of clean energy. At the meeting, Minister Sidhu promoted Canada's successful nuclear energy program, based on the unique heavy water natural uranium reactor system, known as CANDU (CANada Deuterium Uranium). In Kielce, Minister Sidhu and Minister McGuinty attended MSPO 2026, where they met with defence industry leaders and formally opened the Canada Pavilion together with Wadysaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence. As this year's lead nation, Canada is showcasing its defence and security capabilities, innovation and industrial expertise at MSPO, one of Europe's premier defence exhibitions. At MSPO 2026, more than 20 memorandums of understanding were signed, supporting future industry collaboration in the growing defence sector. This momentum is also reflected in trade figures, with Canadian defence exports to Europe increasing by 56% in the last year. With a Team Canada approach, Canada's presence at MSPO 2026 included more than 200 organizations and nearly 500 delegates from Canada's industry and all levels of government, making it the country's largest defence and security business mission worldwide and the largest business delegation Canada has ever brought to Poland. This included 20 economic development organizations from across the country, which participated in more than 200 pre-arranged meetings with international companies to promote Canada as a competitive destination for investment and attract job-creating investment. The ministers' participation highlighted Canada's commitment to expanding commercial and industrial cooperation with partners across Central and Eastern Europe. Canada's involvement at MSPO supports Canada's broader Defence Industrial Strategy, as well as efforts to diversify and strengthen international partnerships and deepen defence industrial cooperation with European partners, including through Canada's participation in the EU's Security Action for Europe (SAFE) initiative. These efforts are also reinforced by Canada's Strategic Exports Office, which helps Canadian businesses pursue major export opportunities in strategic sectors, including defence and security.
